12beb72a5d.why: Fixed: the phrase entered the Origin in its fifth edition, 1869, ten years after 1859 (Spencer coined it in 1864; Darwin's first use in print, 1868, is not contradicted now).

Broccoli from flower heads; cabbage terminal bud, kohlrabi stem, Brussels sprouts axillary buds; one species; charlock is the plant usually called wild mustard. No T1/T2 question uses these crops.

330e731ee4.why: No longer repeats the pigeon question's one-ancestor fact: now the classify task (a person choosing the parents against the heat doing the choosing), not taught at T2. All three distractors give a live people- or gene-based reason; the key's reason teaches the term. Wayne (Vila et al. 1997) and Lorenz's jackals in the context are right. The hot-city strays read as part of the supposed case.

d5dda55a37.why: 'Soaking the seeds' replaces roasting, so the misconception (the surroundings change the gene) is live without a dead seed. Teosinte, tga1, about 9,000 years ago in southwestern Mexico: true.

b6d06f1cfe.why: The contagion choice also explains speed, so the key is no longer the only speed answer; it is false (resistance is inherited). 'Pass through many generations a year' fixes the voice. DDT, resistance in Europe by 1947, 7-10 days egg to adult, more than 500 insect kinds: true.

Paint under the wings, Birmingham soot, Dorset lichen, two to three times as many pale recaptured in Dorset, Tinbergen's film, 98 in 100 by 1895: true.

a6bc268145.why: No longer repeats 388aa73b3e's fact, and the weak bat choice is gone: it now asks what the re-test meant for the critics' charge, and the result is not in the stem. Critics (trunk sites, inflated densities), six years near Cambridge, a dozen moths a night on branches, over half of wild moths resting on branches, nine bird species, published 2012: true.

969af57aff.why: Key matches the sources (roses lack the F3'5'H gene for delphinidin; bred 'blue' roses are lilac, lavender or violet). Distractors are honest wrong ideas built on the T3 Mendel unit (hidden recessive, blending) plus not enough generations; parallel and live. Florigene and Suntory's pansy gene and lavender-mauve result: true. Seventh-grade (MS-LS4-5), not a T1/T2 fact. Minor: trace rosacyanin pigments in a few roses, and new mutations over long spans, make the context's 'can never turn up' a crossing-scale simplification, still true for breeding.
